transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I'm a firefighter, and when I’m not on an actual call, I just can’t keep my attention on training, reports, or manuals long enough to get through them properly. It's starting to hold me back from a promotion I'm working toward, so I really need to figure out what's going on.
In addition to trouble focusing, have you been feeling unusually restless, on edge, or unable to relax during times when you're not on duty?

Yes, absolutely. Even on my days off, I can't just sit and watch a movie with my son without getting edgy and bored within minutes, so I'm constantly fiddling with my phone or getting up. I always have this pent-up, restless feeling like I need to be moving, pacing, or organizing things, and I only really relax when I'm completely exhausted.
Have there been times when you felt down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks or more?

No, I haven't really felt down, sad, or hopeless like that. My main struggles are really just with staying focused, feeling constantly restless, and managing my attention, rather than feeling depressed.
When did you first start noticing these attention and restlessness issues—were they present since childhood, or did they begin more recently in adulthood?

These issues became impossible to ignore about a year and a half ago when I started my captaincy coursework, but they actually go back to childhood. Even in elementary school, my teachers constantly moved my seat because I wouldn't stop talking, and I'd forget to turn in homework. My report cards always said I was smart but just couldn't sit still or stay focused.

The absence of depressive symptoms rules out a depressive disorder, and the chronic course since childhood is not consistent with adult-onset anxiety as a primary issue.
